title: Implement CY‑EAM and CY‑XEAM2 potentials
action: Write code to implement the Cai‑Ye EAM (CY‑EAM) and the CY‑XEAM2 extended EAM potentials for platinum. The total energy, electron density, embedding function, pair potential, and the XEAM asymmetric density correction must be correctly computed. Verify correctness by checking energy and forces on a simple test configuration (e.g., a platinum dimer at the bulk nearest-neighbour distance).
description: Process step that produces the potential implementations used in all subsequent property calculations.

title: Compute bulk properties
action: Using the implemented potentials, compute for both CY‑EAM and CY‑XEAM2: (i) equilibrium fcc lattice constant and cohesive energy by relaxing the primitive cell; (ii) unrelaxed vacancy formation energy from a supercell with one atom removed; (iii) elastic constants C11, C12, C44. Report all values in a JSON file.
description: JSON file containing the computed bulk properties for both potentials.
output_schema: Object with keys "CY‑EAM" and "CY‑XEAM2". Each value is an object with keys: "lattice_constant_A" (float, Å), "cohesive_energy_eV" (float, eV/atom), "vacancy_formation_energy_eV" (float, eV), "C11_GPa" (float), "C12_GPa" (float), "C44_GPa" (float).

title: Compute cluster properties
action: Relax the geometries of a platinum dimer, trimer, and tetrahedron using both potentials. For each cluster, extract the binding energy per atom and the average bond length. Report the results for both potentials in a JSON file.
description: JSON file containing the relaxed cluster properties for both potentials. This artifact is load-bearing: correct values require a functional potential implementation, thus forcing execution of the preceding process step.
output_schema: Object with keys "CY‑EAM" and "CY‑XEAM2". Each value is an object with keys "dimer", "trimer", "tetrahedron". Each cluster object has keys: "bond_length_A" (float, Å) and "binding_energy_eV_per_atom" (float, eV/atom).

title: Compute surface properties
action: For both potentials, calculate the clean (111) and (100) surface energies using slab models. Compute the diffusion barrier of a single platinum adatom on the Pt(111) surface by evaluating the total energy at the fcc and saddle adsorption sites. Report the results in a JSON file.
description: JSON file containing the surface energies and adatom diffusion barrier for both potentials.
output_schema: Object with keys "CY‑EAM" and "CY‑XEAM2". Each value is an object with keys: "surface_energy_111_eV_per_A2" (float, eV/Å²), "surface_energy_100_eV_per_A2" (float, eV/Å²), "adatom_diffusion_barrier_eV" (float, eV).
